scope: Q1:B0 only; four texts, all sections, complete visible and JSON questions, and supplied theory excerpt reviewed. No code run.

options.label: A
options.wrong_model: Deliberate inversion of isolation/sharing; plausible novice misconception.
options.sections: Generally refute the inversion; claim synchronized unnecessary if isolated is an appropriate reductio. No issue requiring hidden assumptions.

options.label: B
options.wrong_model: Equates Java Process and Thread APIs; ProcessBuilder wrapper wording is an inaccurate but plausible confusion.
options.sections: Consistently separates native Process from JVM Thread; examples are somewhat informal but support misconception.

options.label: C
options.sections: Core memory distinction correct. Explanation's claim switching is cheaper because no page-table change/TLB flush and example fixed microseconds vs milliseconds are unsupported absolutes; costs depend on runtime/platform. Edge claim about an uncaught worker exception killing the JVM is misleading: ordinary uncaught exception terminates that thread; JVM shutdown depends on remaining non-daemon threads etc.

options.label: D
options.wrong_model: Confuses Unix process fork/copy model with Java thread creation; coherent wrong answer.
options.sections: Refutes the error accurately; fork is an OS process-creation concept, not Java Thread.start mechanism.

CONTENT.reason: Each option addresses the requested process/thread distinction through isolation/shared memory or explicit equivalence claim.

FACTS.reason: C sections contain unsupported cost/TLB absolutes and misleading claim that an uncaught exception may kill the JVM; option core itself is correct.

LINKAGE.reason: C explanation/example/edge_cases add claims beyond the supported central distinction; API citations support ProcessBuilder and Thread roles, not performance numbers.

SECTIONS.reason: C edge_cases conflates worker-thread termination with JVM termination; example's fixed timings are not general facts.

SFPL.reason: All four are single-sentence prose comparisons of similar length and punctuation; no clear length/format cue. C's sections do not affect visible option-form verdict.

ANSC.reason: All four make a complete, self-contained claim about the distinction; wrong answers present plausible errors rather than an omission.

RU.reason: Russian is clear; technical terms/API names are conventional, with minor English jargon consistent across options.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Universal cheaper-switching/page-table/TLB assertion not established; implementation and platform dependent.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Fixed Thread/fork creation times are unsupported as general values.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Uncaught exception normally ends its thread; without an uncaught handler does not by itself kill JVM.

sources.verified: Process controls native processes created by ProcessBuilder.start/Runtime.exec.
Thread is execution in a program; uncaught completion terminates the thread; platform threads typically map 1:1 to kernel threads.
JVM abstract run-time data areas: heap shared among threads; stacks and pc registers per-thread.
Static fields belong to class declarations; no per-thread copies implied.

limits: Primary Java 21 API/JVMS/JLS pages checked. No code or performance benchmark run. Performance and TLB statements are not treated as established universal facts. Does not review other questions or constitute FINAL/whole-file acceptance.
